name: CT-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joe Courtney has a large cash advantage ($603K vs $125K) and no outside opposition spending
District leans Democratic with a +4 partisan lean and a favorable national environment for Democrats
Prediction markets price Courtney near certain to win
No public polling in the race, so uncertainty rests on fundamentals alone
model.rationale: Courtney combines incumbency, a Democratic-leaning district, a roughly 2-to-1 fundraising edge, and near-certain pricing on prediction markets, with no outside spending against him. Challenger George Austin's modest warchest gives little sign of a serious threat.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Courtney or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Eastern Connecticut's 2nd District has reelected Democrat Joe Courtney repeatedly, and he returns this cycle with the advantages of incumbency in a seat that leans Democratic by about four points. The national environment also favors his party, adding to a fundamentals picture that points comfortably his way.

Republican George Austin has raised about $314,000, a respectable sum for a challenger but far short of Courtney's $760,000, and Courtney holds a wide cash-on-hand lead with no outside groups opposing him. Prediction markets price Courtney's chances at roughly 97 percent. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on these fundamentals, which consistently point to a safe Democratic hold in the mid-to-high teens margin range.
